_comment: Reproduces the ONE alias bug class the pre-scan exists for, with entirely generic names. The shape that matters: a bare logical group ('theme') EXISTS alongside slash-qualified mode groups ('theme/light', 'theme/dark'), and two aliases WRITTEN ON THE BARE GROUP point at a path under it that has no token there. A naive 'is the head segment missing?' check would not catch this, because 'theme' is present — which is precisely why the pre-scan resolves the whole path instead. Two bad aliases, not one, so the 'reports ALL of them in a single pass' contract is actually exercised. The referencing tokens sit on the bare group deliberately: a token inside 'theme/light' writing this same alias is the sibling-mode-set shape the engine now resolves on its own (#564, tokens-mode-set-alias.json), so it would produce no diagnostic and this fixture would test nothing.

accent.$description: Mode-independent, so it lives on the bare group. Its presence is the point: the bare group is real.

color.$description: BROKEN: a mode-independent token reaching for a mode-scoped path. 'theme.border' has no token, and the bare group has no mode to fold to.
BROKEN in the same way, so the pre-scan must report both in one pass rather than aborting on the first.
